transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

Lately I can’t think clearly or concentrate the way I used to at work, and it feels like my mind just won’t stay organized. It's making it really hard to do my job at the salon, and I just feel completely overwhelmed by it.
Have you been feeling sad or losing interest in things most days, or is the main problem worry and feeling overwhelmed?

It’s definitely more of a deep sadness and feeling blank rather than just being worried. It feels like this heavy gray cloud is sitting on my chest all the time, and I wake up feeling completely empty. I've lost interest in almost everything, and I can't even bring myself to care about seeing my friends anymore.
How long have you been feeling this sad, empty, and losing interest in things—has it been most days for at least two weeks, or did it start after a specific stressful event?

I've felt consistently low and empty most days for a little over a year now, so it's definitely been much longer than just two weeks. It started gradually after my first few months of working full-time at the salon, as the pressure there really began to pile up.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 months when you felt back to your usual self, or has this low mood been present most days for more than a year without much relief?

No, I haven't had a period of two months where I felt back to my usual self. I've felt consistently low, empty, and weighed down most days for a little over a year now. I can only really recall a few brief weeks at a time when I didn't feel deeply down and guilty.
Have you also had changes in sleep, appetite, energy, or feelings of low self-worth during this time?

Yes, my appetite is completely gone and my clothes are getting loose because I have to force myself to eat toast, and at night I just lie awake staring at the ceiling. I constantly feel like I'm moving underwater, dragging a hundred pounds just to do basic tasks. I also keep replaying all my past mistakes, feeling like I don't deserve my job or my friends and that I'm just ruining everyone's life.
Have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself or ending your life?

Yes, there are nights when I lie in bed staring at the ceiling, thinking it would be better if I just didn't wake up. I've caught myself picturing how easy it would be to step in front of a train or take all my medications at once. But actually doing something like that still really scares me.
Have you ever had a period of several days or longer when you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, and were more talkative or impulsive than normal?

No, I've never experienced anything like that. It has actually been the complete opposite for me, where I just feel incredibly drained and slowed down all the time. I've never had periods where I felt energized or didn't need sleep.
Have these symptoms caused a marked drop in your ability to work, take care of yourself, or function in daily life, and have they been present nearly every day for at least two years?

Yes, it has caused a massive drop in my functioning—I've had to cut my hours at the salon after being written up for mistakes, stopped seeing my friends, and some days I can't even manage to shower. This has been going on for almost two years now, ever since I started working full-time, and it feels like my mind hasn't gone back to how it used to be.

Have you ever had a stretch of at least 2 months during this time when your mood and interest were back to normal, or has the depression been present most days for at least 2 years without much relief?

No, I definitely haven't had a stretch of two months where my mood was back to normal, and I can only remember a few brief weeks at a time when I didn't feel deeply down, empty, and guilty. While my overall struggles started about two years ago when I transitioned to full-time work, this consistent heavy, sad mood has been present most days for a little over a year now.
Before this year of feeling depressed most days, was there a period of at least 2 years when you felt low or down for most days but not as severely as now?

No, I didn't have a period of feeling low like that before this started. My mood difficulties and struggles only began about two years ago when I transitioned from cosmetology school to working full-time at the salon. Before that, I was actually doing okay.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets criteria for a severe depressive episode: persistent depressed mood and marked anhedonia for over a year, with neurovegetative symptoms (insomnia, poor appetite/weight loss, low energy, psychomotor slowing, poor concentration, excessive guilt/worthlessness), significant functional impairment, and suicidal ideation with method thoughts. There is no history of manic/hypomanic episodes. The course is prolonged, but the interview does not establish a prior distinct depressive episode with full remission, making recurrent depression less supported than a single severe episode.
